Home.title: Teaching Workload Distributor
Home.subtitle: A Tabu Search-based tool for optimized faculty allocation

about.title: About the Project
about.p1: This project is part of a Master's research developed at the Institute of Mathematics and Computer Sciences (ICMC) of the University of São Paulo (USP). The goal is to develop a computational tool to assist in the process of assigning teachers to classes, considering preferences, scheduling constraints, and teaching workload balance.
about.p2: The tool uses the Tabu Search metaheuristic to find high-quality solutions to this combinatorial optimization problem, which is known for its computational complexity.

items.f1: Automatic assignment of teachers to classes using Tabu Search
items.f2: Consideration of teachers' preferences and priorities
items.f7: Analysis of teachers' teaching workload balance

Accessibility.subtitle: Learn about the accessibility features available in this tool and how to use them

intro.title: Our Commitment to Accessibility
intro.p1: We are committed to ensuring that this tool is accessible to all users, regardless of their abilities or limitations. We follow the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 to ensure an inclusive experience.
intro.p2: This page describes the accessibility features available and how to use them to improve your experience with the application.

Constraints.assignmentWithoutFormsDescription: This constraint checks if the professor filled out the form for the subjects they were assigned.
Constraints.validateLocksDescription: Constraint that prevents changes to locked cells.
Constraints.classWithoutTeacherDescription: Constraint that prevents classes from remaining without an assigned professor.
Constraints.scheduleConflictDescription: This constraint checks if professors were assigned to subjects that occur at the same time or have overlapping start and end times.
Constraints.minimumTeachingLoadDescription: Penalizes the solution evaluation for each professor who has not reached the minimum assigned teaching load.
Constraints.maximumTeachingLoadDescription: Penalizes the solution evaluation for each professor who has exceeded the assigned teaching load limit.

Movements.addDescription: Adding a professor to a class.
Movements.removeDescription: Removing a professor from a class

StopCriteria.iterationLimitDescription: Function that will stop the algorithm if a certain number of iterations is reached.
StopCriteria.iterationsWithoutModificationDescription: Function that will stop the algorithm if a certain number of iterations without modification of the best solution is reached.
StopCriteria.iterationsWithoutImprovementInEvaluation: Function that stops the algorithm's execution if the solution evaluations do not show improvement over a certain number of iterations.

AspirationCriteria.objectiveDescription: The tabu will be broken if the observed solution presents an objective value higher than the best global solution found.
AspirationCriteria.sameEvaluationDescription: This criterion aims to accept solutions with an objective value (evaluation) greater than or equal to the global best after a certain number of iterations without modification of the best neighbor. The goal is to make symmetrical solutions (with the same evaluation but different assignments) the global best, encouraging the search for better neighborhoods.

ObjectiveComponent.maximizeprioritiesDescription: Maximizes the overall satisfaction of professors, prioritizing assignments where there is a higher declared preference in the intention forms.
ObjectiveComponent.weightedprioritiesDescription: Similar to standard maximization, but uses a non-linear weight scale (e.g., exponential) to disproportionately value meeting the professor's top options (Top-N).
ObjectiveComponent.minimizeDifferenceBetweenBalancesDescrip: Seeks to reduce the variability of historical balances among professors, penalizing scenarios where some accumulate significant credit while others accumulate significant debt.
ObjectiveComponent.maximizePrioritiesUsingBalancesDescripti: Weights the professor's preference by their current balance. Professors with a greater need for workload (debt balance) have their priorities amplified in the competition for classes.
ObjectiveComponent.minimizeDifferenceInTeachingLoadDescript: Focuses on equity for the current semester, minimizing absolute deviations of the load assigned to each professor relative to the overall average of distributed credits.
ObjectiveComponent.minimizeBalanceUtilizationDescription: Optimizes the assignment by avoiding assigning classes to professors with high positive balances, preserving the long-term hour bank balance (Minimizes Multiplier * Balance * Load).
